title: Learn to Read Tarot
introduction: Seven practical tutorials for preparing a reading, using each spread, and connecting the cards.

articles.title: Prepare a Reading
articles.summary: Choose a question, select the spread, and prepare the deck before you draw.

sections.heading: Choose the Focus
sections.body: Decide what you want to ask or explore. Keep the question short enough to remember while you shuffle.

sections.heading: Choose the Spread
sections.body: Select One Card or a three-card spread. Read the position names first so every card has a clear role.

sections.heading: Shuffle and Draw
sections.body: Shuffle while holding the question in mind. Draw the cards in position order, then reveal and read them one by one.

articles.title: One Card Focus
articles.summary: Use one card to find the main idea or influence around your question.

sections.heading: What It Is For
sections.body: Use this reading when you want one clear focus rather than a full three-card spread.

sections.heading: Draw the Card
sections.body: Hold the question in mind, shuffle, draw one card, and turn it face up.

sections.heading: Read the Message
sections.body: Notice the image and keywords, then connect the upright meaning directly to your question.

articles.title: Past, Present, Possible Direction
articles.summary: Read what shaped the situation, what is active now, and where it is heading.

sections.heading: The Three Positions
sections.body: Card 1 is the Past, card 2 is the Present, and card 3 is the Possible Direction.

sections.heading: Lay Out the Cards
sections.body: Shuffle and draw three cards from left to right, keeping each card in its assigned position.

sections.heading: Read the Sequence
sections.body: Read each position first, then notice what continues or changes from the first card to the third.

articles.title: Situation, Challenge, Guidance
articles.summary: See the issue, the main obstacle or influence, and the guidance offered by the spread.

sections.heading: The Three Positions
sections.body: Card 1 is the Situation, card 2 is the Challenge, and card 3 is the Guidance.

sections.heading: Lay Out the Cards
sections.body: Ask about the issue, then shuffle and draw three cards from left to right.

sections.heading: Connect the Reading
sections.body: Read how the challenge affects the situation and how the guidance responds to both cards.

articles.title: You, Other Person, Connection
articles.summary: Explore your role, the other person's role, and the connection between you.

sections.heading: The Three Positions
sections.body: Card 1 represents You, card 2 the Other Person, and card 3 the Connection.

sections.heading: Lay Out the Cards
sections.body: Think of the relationship, then shuffle and draw three cards from left to right.

sections.heading: Read the Dynamic
sections.body: Compare the first two cards and use the third to describe the connection they form together.

articles.title: For, Against, and Outcome
articles.summary: Use three cards to read one clear yes-or-no question.

sections.heading: Ask the Question
sections.body: Choose one clear question that can be answered with yes or no, and keep it in mind while shuffling.

sections.heading: Lay Out the Cards
sections.body: Draw from left to right: card 1 is For and supports yes, card 2 is Against and supports no, and card 3 is the Outcome.

sections.heading: Read the Outcome
sections.body: Read the Outcome card together with the For and Against cards to form the final answer to the spread.

articles.title: Read Symbols and the Whole Spread
articles.summary: Connect visible symbols, card meanings, and positions into one complete reading.

sections.heading: Observe Each Card
sections.body: Look at the figures, objects, colors, numbers, and direction of movement before reading the reference meaning.

sections.heading: Compare the Cards
sections.body: Notice repeated suits, numbers, symbols, moods, or contrasts across the spread.

sections.heading: Summarize the Spread
sections.body: Bring the positions and repeated details together in one or two sentences that answer the original question.
